title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election for Colorado's 6th Congressional District
description: The 2026 election for Colorado's 6th Congressional District will determine who represents the district covering Aurora and parts of Arapahoe, Adams, and Douglas Counties in the U.S. House of Representatives. Incumbent Democrat Jason Crow, first elected in 2018 when he flipped the seat, is seeking a fifth term. The Democratic primary is uncontested, while Republican Mel Tewahade is the sole Republican primary candidate. The primary election is scheduled for June 30, 2026, and the general election is on November 3, 2026. The district has trended Democratic in recent cycles and is rated as Solid/Safe Democratic by major nonpartisan forecasters.

candidates.name: Jason Crow
candidates.summary: Jason Crow is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Colorado's 6th Congressional District, first elected in 2018. He is a former U.S. Army Ranger who served in Iraq with the 82nd Airborne Division and later with the 75th Ranger Regiment, and worked as an attorney prior to his congressional service. In Congress, he has focused on national security, veterans' affairs, and gun safety legislation.

candidates.name: Mel Tewahade
candidates.summary: Mel Tewahade is the Republican candidate challenging incumbent Jason Crow for Colorado's 6th Congressional District. He is the founder and CEO of Infinity Wealth Management Inc., a financial planning firm, and has over three decades of experience in the life insurance and financial services industry. Tewahade is an Ethiopian-American, a cancer survivor, and has also worked as a documentary filmmaker.

forecast.rationale: There is no district-level polling in the provided data, which limits precision and keeps confidence at medium rather than high. However, the non-polling signals are strongly consistent: incumbent Democrat Jason Crow has held this seat since flipping it in 2018, the district is described as having trended Democratic in recent cycles, and major nonpartisan forecasters rate it Solid/Safe Democratic. Crow's primary is uncontested, and no strong Republican or third-party challenge is indicated in the data. Given these fundamentals, Democrats have an overwhelming advantage in this district, supporting a safe_d rating with approximately 96% win probability and an estimated margin of roughly 12 percentage points, consistent with Crow's recent re-election margins.
